samasa.type: karmadhāraya (sarva 'whole, entire' qualifying aruṇā)
samasa.vigraha: सर्वा अरुणा सर्वारुणा
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarvā aruṇā sarvāruṇā
samasa.explanation: sarva in the sense 'whole, in every part' qualifies aruṇā 'red'; aruṇā is the head and the compound describes Her: red throughout. sarvā takes its masculine stem sarva inside the karmadhāraya (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42).

names.meaning: She who is red in every part
names.significance: Her body, garments, garlands and ornaments are all red, as the dhyāna verses picture Her (aruṇāṃ …; aruṇa-mālya-bhūṣāmbarām). In Śrīvidyā this red is read as vimarśa, the self-reflective power of consciousness, and as the color of compassion.

meaning_check.note: Not only Her complexion: the name says She is red throughout, and the dhyāna verses extend it to Her garments, garlands and ornaments.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner nañ-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: न अवद्यम् अनवद्यम्; अनवद्यानि अङ्गानि यस्याः सा अनवद्याङ्गी
samasa.vigraha_iast: na avadyam anavadyam; anavadyāni aṅgāni yasyāḥ sā anavadyāṅgī
samasa.explanation: (1) an-avadya 'not blameworthy, faultless' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; na appears as an- before a vowel, Pāṇini 6.3.73–74). (2) It qualifies aṅga 'limb', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose limbs are faultless'. aṅga, a body-part word ending the bahuvrīhi, takes the feminine ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54): -aṅgī.

components.note: the negative na, as an- before a vowel
lit. 'not to be spoken (of)'; Pāṇini 3.1.101 gives avadya in the sense 'to be censured'
aṅga, with the feminine ī of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose every limb is faultless
names.significance: No flaw can be found in any part of Her form; traditionally this is read also as freedom from every impurity, since Her body is pure consciousness.

meaning_check.note: anavadya means 'faultless, blameless', not 'worthy of worship'; the previous meaning did not follow from the word.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: सर्वाणि आभरणानि सर्वाभरणानि; सर्वाभरणैः भूषिता सर्वाभरणभूषिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarvāṇi ābharaṇāni sarvābharaṇāni; sarvābharaṇaiḥ bhūṣitā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-ābharaṇa 'all ornaments' (karmadhāraya). (2) The participle bhūṣitā 'adorned' is the head and takes the ornaments in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who is adorned with all ornaments
names.significance: The description of Her form closes by gathering every ornament into one; in worship the ornaments (ābharaṇa) are offered to Her as one of the services of pūjā.

meaning_check.note: 'resplendent' and 'all types of' tightened to the participle bhūṣitā 'adorned' and sarva 'all'.

names.previous_split_issues: sarvābharaṇa was left as one row (sarva + ābharaṇa).

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: शिवः कामेश्वरः शिवकामेश्वरः; शिवकामेश्वरस्य अङ्कः शिवकामेश्वराङ्कः; शिवकामेश्वराङ्के तिष्ठति इति शिवकामेश्वराङ्कस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: śivaḥ kāmeśvaraḥ śivakāmeśvaraḥ; śivakāmeśvarasya aṅkaḥ śivakāmeśvarāṅkaḥ; śivakāmeśvarāṅke tiṣṭhati iti śivakāmeśvarāṅkasthā
samasa.explanation: (1) śiva-kāmeśvara 'Śiva who is Kāmeśvara' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) …kāmeśvara-aṅka 'His lap' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) -stha 'staying, seated' is √sthā with the suffix -a after a word in the locative (Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ), an upapada-tatpuruṣa; it takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who sits on the lap of Śiva, who is Kāmeśvara
names.significance: Her iconic form is seated on the left lap of Kāmeśvara: Śiva and Śakti as one, never apart. Traditionally the name is read as that inseparability, the stillness of Śiva holding the dynamism of Śakti.

meaning_check.note: 'conqueror of desire' is an interpretation, not the word: Kāmeśvara is 'Lord of desire' and is named, not glossed; 'shiva' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: kāmeśvarāṅka was left as one row (kāmeśvara + aṅka; kāmeśvara is itself kāma + īśvara).

components.meaning: the auspicious one; the consort of Śiva

names.meaning: She who is Śivā, auspiciousness itself, the power of Śiva
names.significance: Traditionally there is no difference between Śiva and Śivā: She is Śiva's own nature, and as the auspicious one She bestows auspiciousness and liberation on those who worship Her.

meaning_check.note: The name is 'the auspicious one' and the feminine of Śiva; 'bestows all that is auspicious' is the traditional consequence, now given under significance.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner saptamī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: स्वस्मिन् अधीनः स्वाधीनः; स्वाधीनः वल्लभः यस्याः सा स्वाधीनवल्लभा
samasa.vigraha_iast: svasmin adhīnaḥ svādhīnaḥ; svādhīnaḥ vallabhaḥ yasyāḥ sā svādhīnavallabhā
samasa.explanation: (1) sva-adhīna 'dependent on oneself, subject to oneself' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa: adhīna 'dependent' governs the locative). Here sva refers to Her. (2) It qualifies vallabha 'beloved, husband', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose beloved is subject to Her'; vallabha takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: vallabha, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who keeps Her husband always under Her control
names.significance: In poetics the svādhīnabhartṛkā is the heroine whose husband is under her sway. Saundaryalaharī 1 gives the reason: Śiva joined to Śakti is able to act; without Her He cannot even stir.
names.previous_split_issues: svādhīna was glossed 'self-dependent/independent'; it means 'dependent on oneself', i.e. subject to Her. svādhīna is sva + adhīna.

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: मध्यम् शृङ्गम् मध्यशृङ्गम्; सुमेरोः मध्यशृङ्गम् सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गम्; सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गे तिष्ठति इति सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: madhyam śṛṅgam madhyaśṛṅgam; sumeroḥ madhyaśṛṅgam sumerumadhyaśṛṅgam; sumerumadhyaśṛṅge tiṣṭhati iti sumerumadhyaśṛṅgasthā
samasa.explanation: (1) madhya-śṛṅga 'the middle peak' (karmadhāraya). (2) sumeru-madhyaśṛṅga 'the middle peak of Sumeru' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) -sthā 'abiding' (√sthā after a word in the locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) is the head: 'She who abides on the middle peak of Sumeru'. The members are simply juxtaposed.

names.meaning: She who sits on the middle peak of Mount Sumeru
names.significance: Traditionally Meru has three peaks at its corners, the seats of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, and a higher middle peak where Her city stands. With this name begins the account of Her abode.

sandhi.rule: nasal assimilation: the final t of śrīmat becomes n before the nasal n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: श्रीमत् नगरम् श्रीमन्नगरम्; श्रीमन्नगरस्य नायिका श्रीमन्नगरनायिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: śrīmat nagaram śrīmannagaram; śrīmannagarasya nāyikā śrīmannagaranāyikā
samasa.explanation: (1) śrīmat-nagara 'the glorious city' (karmadhāraya), i.e. Śrīnagara or Śrīpura, Her city. (2) nāyikā 'mistress, sovereign' is the head and the city stands to it in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is the sovereign of the glorious city (Śrīpura)
names.significance: Śrīpura, the city on Meru's central peak, is described in the Lalitopākhyāna with its many concentric enclosures; in Śrīvidyā the city is also the Śrīcakra, with Her at its center.

meaning_check.note: The previous meaning broke off ('the Mistress of the most auspicious (or prosperous)') and omitted nagara 'city'.

names.previous_split_issues: 'śrīman' was given in its sandhi form; the stem is śrīmat (t becomes n before nagara).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: चिन्तामणिमयम् गृहम् चिन्तामणिगृहम्; चिन्तामणिगृहस्य अन्तः चिन्तामणिगृहान्तः; चिन्तामणिगृहान्ते तिष्ठति इति चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: cintāmaṇimayam gṛham cintāmaṇigṛham; cintāmaṇigṛhasya antaḥ cintāmaṇigṛhāntaḥ; cintāmaṇigṛhānte tiṣṭhati iti cintāmaṇigṛhāntasthā
samasa.explanation: (1) cintāmaṇi-gṛha 'the house made of cintāmaṇi gems' (karmadhāraya with 'made of' understood). (2) …gṛha-anta 'its interior' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) -sthā 'abiding' (√sthā after a word in the locative) is the head.

components.note: cintā 'thought' + maṇi 'gem': the gem that grants what is thought of

names.meaning: She who dwells within the palace built of cintāmaṇi, the wish-fulfilling gems
names.significance: The cintāmaṇi palace is the innermost dwelling within Śrīpura. In Śrīvidyā the city and its palace correspond to the Śrīcakra, the palace to its innermost region.

meaning_check.note: 'within' (anta) added; ITRANS 'chintAmaNi' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: gṛhāntasthā was left as one row (gṛha + anta + sthā).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a dvigu)
samasa.vigraha: पञ्च ब्रह्माणः पञ्चब्रह्माणः; पञ्चब्रह्मात्मकम् आसनम् पञ्चब्रह्मासनम्; पञ्चब्रह्मासने स्थिता पञ्चब्रह्मासनस्थिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañca brahmāṇaḥ pañcabrahmāṇaḥ; pañcabrahmātmakam āsanam pañcabrahmāsanam; pañcabrahmāsane sthitā pañcabrahmāsanasthitā
samasa.explanation: (1) pañca-brahman 'the five Brahmas', a numeral compound used as a fixed designation (dvigu). (2) …brahma-āsana 'the seat formed of the five Brahmas' (karmadhāraya with 'consisting of' understood). (3) The participle sthitā 'seated' is the head and takes the seat in the locative. pañcan and brahman lose their final n in composition; these are morphological, not sandhi.

components.note: appears as pañca- in the compound

components.meaning: Brahman; here the five 'Brahmas', the five lords of the cosmic functions
components.note: appears as brahma- in the compound

names.meaning: She who is seated on the throne formed of the five Brahmas
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the throne's four legs are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara, and Sadāśiva is its seat: the lords of creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment and grace all serve as Her throne.

meaning_check.note: 'BrahmAs' put into IAST; the seat is formed of the five Brahmas.

names.previous_split_issues: brahmāsana was glossed 'seat of Brahma'; it is the seat formed of the five Brahmas (brahman + āsana), not Brahmā's seat.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
the m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: पद्मानाम् अटवी पद्माटवी; महती पद्माटवी महापद्माटवी; महापद्माटव्याम् संतिष्ठते इति महापद्माटवीसंस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: padmānām aṭavī padmāṭavī; mahatī padmāṭavī mahāpadmāṭavī; mahāpadmāṭavyām saṃtiṣṭhate iti mahāpadmāṭavīsaṃsthā
samasa.explanation: (1) padma-aṭavī 'a forest of lotuses' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) mahā qualifies it, 'the great lotus forest' (karmadhāraya; mahatī → mahā-, Pāṇini 6.3.42 and 6.3.46). It can equally be read as mahāpadma-aṭavī 'the forest of great lotuses'. (3) saṃsthā 'abiding' (sam + √sthā + -a, after a word in the locative) is the head.

names.meaning: She who resides in the great lotus forest
names.significance: A great lotus forest is part of the setting of Her city. Traditionally it is also read inwardly, as the lotuses of the yogic body and above all the thousand-petalled lotus at the crown.
names.previous_split_issues: padmāṭavī was left as one row (padma + aṭavī).
names.uncertain: mahā may qualify the forest ('the great lotus forest') or the lotuses ('the forest of great lotuses'); both readings are current and the sense is the same.

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: कदम्बानाम् वनम् कदम्बवनम्; कदम्बवने वसति इति कदम्बवनवासिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kadambānām vanam kadambavanam; kadambavane vasati iti kadambavanavāsinī
samasa.explanation: (1) kadamba-vana 'the forest of kadamba trees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) vāsin 'dwelling', √vas with the suffix -in after a word in the locative (Pāṇini 3.2.78 supy ajātau ṇinis tācchīlye: one whose nature it is to dwell there), is the head; it takes the feminine ī. The members are simply juxtaposed.

components.meaning: the kadamba tree (Neolamarckia cadamba), with fragrant ball-shaped orange flowers

names.meaning: She who resides in the kadamba forest
names.significance: A grove of kadamba trees surrounds Her palace in Śrīpura. On earth, Madurai, the seat of Mīnākṣī, was anciently a kadamba forest, and the Goddess there is traditionally praised by this name.
names.previous_split_issues: kadamba was glossed 'kadamba flower'; here it is the tree, whose groves make the forest.

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: सुधायाः सागरः सुधासागरः; सुधासागरस्य मध्यम् सुधासागरमध्यम्; सुधासागरमध्ये तिष्ठति इति सुधासागरमध्यस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: sudhāyāḥ sāgaraḥ sudhāsāgaraḥ; sudhāsāgarasya madhyam sudhāsāgaramadhyam; sudhāsāgaramadhye tiṣṭhati iti sudhāsāgaramadhyasthā
samasa.explanation: (1) sudhā-sāgara 'the ocean of nectar' and …sāgara-madhya 'its middle' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) -sthā 'abiding' (√sthā after a word in the locative) is the head. The members are simply juxtaposed.

names.meaning: She who resides in the center of the ocean of nectar
names.significance: Traditionally Her city is also placed on an island of gems (maṇidvīpa) in the midst of an ocean of nectar. Inwardly the nectar is read as the amṛta that flows from the thousand-petalled lotus.
names.previous_split_issues: madhyasthā was left as one row (madhya + sthā).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (with the compound-final suffix ṣac)
samasa.vigraha: कामे कमनीये अक्षिणी यस्याः सा कामाक्षी; अथवा कामः अक्ष्णोः यस्याः सा कामाक्षी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāme kamanīye akṣiṇī yasyāḥ sā kāmākṣī; athavā kāmaḥ akṣṇoḥ yasyāḥ sā kāmākṣī
samasa.explanation: A bahuvrīhi describing Her. akṣi 'eye' at the end of a bahuvrīhi becomes akṣa (the samāsānta suffix ṣac, Pāṇini 5.4.113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac) and takes the feminine ī: -ākṣī. kāma may be the adjective 'lovely, desirable' ('whose eyes are lovely') or the noun 'love, desire' ('in whose eyes love dwells').

components.note: akṣi, as akṣa at the end of the bahuvrīhi, with the feminine ī

names.meaning: She whose eyes are lovely, eyes in which love dwells
names.significance: Kāmākṣī is the Goddess of Kāñcīpuram, traditionally identified with Lalitā. A traditional reading divides kā (Sarasvatī) + mā (Lakṣmī) + akṣī: She whose two eyes are Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī.

meaning_check.note: The two alternatives are merged into one sentence that follows the bahuvrīhi; 'awaken desire' goes beyond the word.

names.uncertain: Several analyses are current: kāma as 'lovely' (the meaning given), as 'love, desire' dwelling in Her eyes, and the traditional kā + mā + akṣī (Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī as Her eyes).

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa
samasa.vigraha: कामान् ददाति इति कामदायिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmān dadāti iti kāmadāyinī
samasa.explanation: dāyin 'giving', √dā with the agent suffix -in (a y is inserted after the root's ā), takes kāma 'desire, wish' as its object; it is the head and takes the feminine ī. The members are simply juxtaposed.

components.meaning: desire, wish; also Kāma, the god of love

names.meaning: She who grants all wishes
names.significance: She fulfills the desires of Her devotees, and traditionally the highest of them, the desire for liberation. kāma can also be the god Kāma: She gave back Kāma, burnt by Śiva's eye, a deed named in name 84.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ṛ → ar (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and a dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: देवाः च ऋषयः च देवर्षयः; देवर्षीणाम् गणाः देवर्षिगणाः; देवर्षिगणानाम् सङ्घातः देवर्षिगणसङ्घातः; देवर्षिगणसङ्घातेन स्तूयमानम् देवर्षिगणसङ्घातस्तूयमानम्; आत्मनः वैभवम् आत्मवैभवम्; देवर्षिगणसङ्घातस्तूयमानम् आत्मवैभवम् यस्याः सा देवर्षिगणसङ्घातस्तूयमानात्मवैभवा
samasa.vigraha_iast: devāḥ ca ṛṣayaḥ ca devarṣayaḥ; devarṣīṇām gaṇāḥ devarṣigaṇāḥ; devarṣigaṇānām saṅghātaḥ devarṣigaṇasaṅghātaḥ; devarṣigaṇasaṅghātena stūyamānam devarṣigaṇasaṅghātastūyamānam; ātmanaḥ vaibhavam ātmavaibhavam; devarṣigaṇasaṅghātastūyamānam ātmavaibhavam yasyāḥ sā devarṣigaṇasaṅghātastūyamānātmavaibhavā
samasa.explanation: (1) deva-ṛṣi 'gods and sages' (dvandva; it can also be read as a karmadhāraya, 'the divine sages'). (2) …ṛṣi-gaṇa 'their hosts' and …gaṇa-saṅghāta 'the assembled multitude of those hosts' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (3) stūyamāna 'being praised', the present passive participle of √stu, takes that multitude as agent in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) ātma-vaibhava 'Her own glory' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (3). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose own glory is being praised by …'; vaibhava takes the feminine -ā.

samasa.vigraha: भण्डस्य पुत्राः भण्डपुत्राः; भण्डपुत्राणाम् वधः भण्डपुत्रवधः; भण्डपुत्रवधे उद्युक्ता भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्ता; भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्ता बाला भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबाला; भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबालायाः विक्रमः भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबालाविक्रमः; तेन नन्दिता भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबालाविक्रमनन्दिता

names.meaning: She who is delighted by the valor of Bālā, intent on slaying the sons of Bhaṇḍa

samasa.vigraha_iast: mantriṇī ca asau ambā ca mantriṇyambā; mantriṇyambayā viracitaḥ mantriṇyambāviracitaḥ; viṣaṅgasya vadhaḥ viṣaṅgavadhaḥ; mantriṇyambāviracitaḥ viṣaṅgavadhaḥ mantriṇyambāviracitaviṣaṅgavadhaḥ; tena toṣitā mantriṇyambāviracitaviṣaṅgavadhatoṣitā
samasa.explanation: (1) mantriṇī-ambā 'Mother Mantriṇī' (karmadhāraya of apposition; as a proper name Mantriṇī keeps its feminine form). (2) viracita 'accomplished' takes her as agent in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) viṣaṅga-vadha 'the slaying of Viṣaṅga' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (2) (karmadhāraya). names.meaning: She who is pleased by the slaying of Viṣaṅga accomplished by Mother Mantriṇī
names.significance: Mantriṇī, the counselor of name 69, also takes the field: in this account she slays Viṣaṅga, one of Bhaṇḍa's two brothers.

samasa.vigraha: विशुक्रस्य प्राणाः विशुक्रप्राणाः; विशुक्रप्राणानाम् हरणम् विशुक्रप्राणहरणम्; वाराह्याः वीर्यम् वाराहीवीर्यम्; विशुक्रप्राणहरणम् वाराहीवीर्यम् विशुक्रप्राणहरणवाराहीवीर्यम्; तेन नन्दिता विशुक्रप्राणहरणवाराहीवीर्यनन्दिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: viśukrasya prāṇāḥ viśukraprāṇāḥ; viśukraprāṇānām haraṇam viśukraprāṇaharaṇam; vārāhyāḥ vīryam vārāhīvīryam; viśukraprāṇaharaṇam vārāhīvīryam viśukraprāṇaharaṇavārāhīvīryam; tena nanditā viśukraprāṇaharaṇavārāhīvīryananditā
samasa.explanation: (1) viśukra-prāṇa 'Viśukra's life-breaths' and …prāṇa-haraṇa 'the taking of them' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) vārāhī-vīrya 'Vārāhī's valor' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) (1) and (2) stand in apposition: the valor that was the taking of Viśukra's life (karmadhāraya). (4) nanditā 'delighted' is the head and takes that valor in the instrumental. haraṇa can also be read as an agent noun, 'taking away', qualifying Vārāhī; the sense is the same. The members are simply juxtaposed.

names.meaning: She who is delighted by the valor of Vārāhī, who took the life of Viśukra
names.significance: Vārāhī is Daṇḍanāthā of name 70, the commander of Her army; here she slays Bhaṇḍa's other brother, Viśukra.

samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmeśvarasya mukham kāmeśvaramukham; kāmeśvaramukhasya ālokaḥ kāmeśvaramukhālokaḥ; kāmeśvaramukhālokena kalpitaḥ kāmeśvaramukhālokakalpitaḥ; gaṇānām īśvaraḥ gaṇeśvaraḥ; śrīmān gaṇeśvaraḥ śrīgaṇeśvaraḥ; kāmeśvaramukhālokakalpitaḥ śrīgaṇeśvaraḥ yayā sā kāmeśvaramukhālokakalpitaśrīgaṇeśvarā
samasa.explanation: (1) kāmeśvara-mukha 'Kāmeśvara's face' and …mukha-āloka 'the look upon that face' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas; the genitive is that of the object looked at). (2) kalpita 'fashioned, brought forth' takes the look as its means in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) gaṇa-īśvara 'lord of the hosts', Gaṇeśa (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), with the honorific śrī (karmadhāraya). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi in the instrumental relation: 'She by whom Śrī Gaṇeśa was brought forth through a look at Kāmeśvara's face'; gaṇeśvara takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who brought forth Śrī Gaṇeśa by a glance at the face of Kāmeśvara
names.significance: In the Lalitopākhyāna Viśukra sets up an obstacle-yantra (jaya-vighna-yantra) that saps Her army's strength; She looks at Kāmeśvara's face, and from that look Mahāgaṇeśa arises to shatter it (the next name).

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha ऽ (') marks the absorbed initial a of anavadyāṅgī

verse_notes.note: Read sarvāruṇā | anavadyāṅgī: the avagraha shows where the second name begins. Names 49–51 close the description of Her form; 52–54 name Her union with Kāmeśvara.

Names 55–61 describe Her abode: the central peak of Meru, the city, the cintāmaṇi palace, the throne of the five Brahmas, the lotus and kadamba forests, the ocean of nectar. In 56 śrīman- is śrīmat with t → n before nagara.
The second half holds three names: sudhāsāgaramadhyasthā (61) | kāmākṣī (62) | kāmadāyinī (63).
Here begins the Bhaṇḍāsura episode of the Lalitopākhyāna, which runs to name 84. Name 64: divide stūyamāna + ātma-vaibhava ('Her own glory'), not stūyamānātma.
Name 67 is one name of two words: …koṭikoṭibhiḥ āvṛtā; the visarga becomes r before ā (koṭibhir āvṛtā).
Names 68–70 name the three chariots of the war: Cakrarāja (Hers), Geyacakra (Mantriṇī's) and Kiricakra (Daṇḍanāthā's).
Name 71: Jvālāmālinikā is the goddess Jvālāmālinī (with -kā), one name, followed by ākṣipta 'raised'; do not divide jvālā | mālinikākṣipta.
Name 73: nityā here names the Nityā goddesses, not 'eternal'.
Name 75 begins mantriṇī + ambā joined by yaṇ (ī → y).
Vārāhī (76) is Daṇḍanāthā of name 70. Name 77 introduces Mahāgaṇeśa, who breaks the obstacle-yantra in the next name.

report.summary: Checked all 29 names of ślokas 21–30 against text.json: sandhi at every member junction (and the prefix junctions sam + sthā, adhi + sthita, puras + kṛtā), a layered samāsa analysis with pausa-form vigraha-vākyas, and the meanings against that analysis. Name 50's meaning was wrong (anavadya is 'faultless', not 'worthy of worship') and 56's was truncated; both were replaced. Several old splits misplaced boundaries (64: stūyamāna | ātma-vaibhava; 71: the goddess-name Jvālāmālinikā cut in two; 67: koṭibhiḥ + āvṛtā is two words, so the name is a phrase, not one compound). No error was found in the Sanskrit; the only external sandhi is sarvāruṇā + anavadyāṅgī in śloka 21.
